diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a direct combination of \Cref{a18} and \Cref{a50}.
When $p_j(z)=z^j$ and $\mu$ is the uniform distribution on an arc of the circle, \Cref{a10} recovers the rate stated in terms of the anti-derivative of $\log\cot(\cdot)$ from \Cref{a1}.

issues.failure_explanation: a18 estimates ||V^{-1}|| via max_k ||L_k|| on supp(nu), while a50 estimates max_k sup_{z in supp(mu)} log L_k(z)/n; the one-line proof of a10 combines them with no hypothesis relating nu and mu. As stated (nu arbitrary), the theorem is false: take p_j(z)=z^j, nu the uniform measure on the full unit circle (so G=I, gamma=1), S equispaced on a half-circle arc, and mu the arc-uniform measure. All hypotheses hold and the error terms are o(1), so a10 asserts log kappa(V)/n -> range of U^mu on the arc = (2Cl(Theta/2)-Cl(Theta))/Theta = 2G/pi for Theta=pi, but the paper's own Theorem a1 gives log kappa/n -> (2/Theta)(Cl(Theta/2)-Cl(pi+Theta/2)) = 4G/pi: the minimum of U^mu over the circle is attained on the complementary arc, outside supp(mu). The remark that a10 'recovers' a1's rate therefore also fails (and independently fails because ||G^{-1}|| for monomials on an arc is exponentially large, so the error term swallows the rate even under the charitable nu=mu reading).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis supp(nu) = supp(mu) (or set nu = mu) so that a18 and a50 can be combined, and delete or correct the remark about recovering a1's rate; alternatively restate the rate as the range of U^mu over supp(nu) and rework a50 to bound the sup over supp(nu).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem a10, the paper's general Vandermonde-like theorem, is false as stated whenever the evaluation measure nu and the approximated measure mu have different supports (in particular in the arc/monomial setting that motivated it), and the claim that it recovers Theorem a1's rate is false. Results a1, a3, a4 are proved independently of a10 and are unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem a10: rate is the range of U^mu on supp(mu), but a18 evaluates Lagrange polynomials on supp(nu); contradicts Theorem a1's rate for arcs
issues.why_classification: The nu = mu restriction is a contained edit that preserves a meaningful tight-rate theorem (e.g., for mu-orthonormal polynomial bases), but it weakens the theorem's scope and forces withdrawal of the advertised recovery of a1; no other labelled results depend on a10.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In addition, by \Cref{a24}, $\Cl(\eps n/2) = \hat C \alpha(1-\alpha) \log (2 / \alpha)$ for some $\hat C \in [1/\pi,2/5]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated membership is false: as alpha -> 0, Cl(alpha*pi) ~ alpha*pi*(1 - log(alpha*pi)), so the ratio tends to pi (~3.14), and at alpha = 1/2 it equals G/((1/4) log 4) ~ 2.64; [1/pi, 2/5] = [0.318, 0.4] contains neither. The true range is roughly [2.6, pi]. The proposition is stated without proof ('we recall the following standard results'), so no proof-inference mechanism applies; the claim is simply numerically wrong. Its only use, in a30, quotes the wrong interval but needs solely that the ratio is bounded between positive absolute constants, so a30's conclusion is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace [1/pi, 2/5] with the correct range (or state that the ratio is bounded between two absolute constants).
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicit constants quoted inside the proof of a30 are wrong; no downstream statement or estimate changes.
issues.title: Proposition a24 item 7: false interval [1/pi, 2/5] for Cl(alpha*pi)/(alpha(1-alpha)log(2/alpha))
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a stated constant whose right order of magnitude is forced; the sole application uses only boundedness, so every claim survives verbatim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $\epsilon >0$ and $(m+1) \epsilon < 2 \pi$. Then
\[
-\sum_{j=1}^m\log\pare{2\sin\frac{\eps j}2}
=
\frac{\Cl(\eps m)}\eps
+\frac12\log\eps
-\frac12\log\pare{\eps m\wedge(2\pi-\eps (m+1))} + O(1).
\]

issues.failure_explanation: In the case eps*m > pi, the proof converts the valid a37-based expression into the displayed closed form via a right-endpoint log approximation of the mean of -log(2 sin(t/2)) over [eps*m, eps*(m+1)]; the error of that step is Theta(log(eps/delta)) for delta = 2pi - eps*(m+1) (the a24(6)-type error eps/(2(2pi-x)) diverges), not O(1). The formula is indeed false as delta -> 0+: with eps = (2pi-delta)/(m+1), the sine product identity prod_{j=1}^m 2 sin(pi*j/(m+1)) = m+1 makes the left side tend to -log(m+1), while the right side tends to +infinity like -(1/2) log delta. The stated hypotheses of a26 ((n+1)eps < 2pi) and of a27's second formula ((n+2)eps < 2pi) include the same bad band, so those statements fail there too. Every actual use avoids the band: a46 assumes 2pi - n*eps > 2eps and a47/a30/a42 assume 2pi - n*eps >= 2 sqrt(eps) (so delta >= eps), and the complementary band 2pi - n*eps <= 2eps is treated separately by a45, so no main result is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the hypotheses of a38/a26/a27 to 2pi - eps*(m+1) bounded below by a multiple of eps (e.g., >= eps), which covers every use; the excluded band is already handled by a45.
issues.overall_effect: The three lemmas are false as stated in the near-full-circle band; nothing downstream is affected because all applications stay in the regime where the formulas hold.
issues.title: Lemma a38 (inherited by a26 and a27): the O(1) error diverges as (m+1)eps -> 2pi
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis addition that is automatically satisfied at every application preserves the method, all conclusions, and the advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then \(g_{\textnormal w}(x)\le U(x)\) on $x\in\pare{\eps n,2\pi}$ and \(g_{\textnormal n}(x)\ge U(x)\) on $x\in\pare{\eps n+\eps,2\pi-\eps}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound asserts sup_{x in (-eps, eps*n+eps)} e^{-2U_k(x)} <= e^{-2g_w(eps*n+eps)} (the displayed e^{2g_w} is a typo for e^{-2g_w}, as the next line confirms). No argument is given, and the paper's tools do not yield it: the parabola bound g_w <= U is only proved on (eps*n, 2pi) (a29), and the factor |(1/2) csc((x-k*eps)/2)| in e^{-2U_k} = (1/4) csc^2((x-k*eps)/2) e^{-2U} is unbounded at x = k*eps inside that interval, so the a42-style pull-out estimate cannot be applied there either. What is missing is a lower bound for U_k on the whole node arc (equivalently a sup bound for |L_k| there), a nontrivial estimate the paper never proves (a26 covers only theta = k*eps, a27 two off-arc points). The bound feeds a32's upper bound, hence a33, and through the xi estimate of a44 both directions of the equispaced equality in a47, and therefore the equality clauses of a1, a3, a4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a lemma bounding max_{x in (-eps, eps*n+eps)} e^{-2U_k(x)} by e^{-2g_w(eps*n+eps)} up to polynomial factors, e.g., by extending the Riemann-sum estimates for U_k to off-node points of the node arc and comparing with the parabola value.
issues.overall_effect: The headline upper bounds (the inequality of a1 and the upper bounds of a3/a4) are unaffected, since they use only the max-based argument via a16, a19, a26; but the matching lower bounds - the 'equality is achieved' clauses of a1, a3, a4, the abstract's exact-rate claim, and the (1.791)^N lower-bound claim - rest on this unproved estimate.
issues.title: Lemma a32's proof asserts without argument that the node-arc integral of e^{-2U_k} is negligible (eq. a43)
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma should suffice (the bound holds with exponential room in the continuum limit), and the paper's principal upper-bound results are independent of it; but the tightness/equality claims of the main theorems currently rest on an unproved nontrivial step.

issues.failure_explanation: Applying a49 at z = z_-^{(k)} with parameter eps' requires eps' <= dist(z_-^{(k)}, supp(mu_k)) = dist(z_-^{(k)}, S\{z_k}), which is never checked and can fail: the minimizer of U^{mu_k} over supp(mu) can lie arbitrarily close to a node (e.g., for equispaced nodes on an arc with mu the arc-uniform measure, the on-arc minimum of U^{mu_k} is attained at distance ~ 1/(n^2 log n) from an endpoint node, far smaller than eps' <= eps). The quoted a49 conclusion is therefore used outside its hypotheses. The sharp inequality can be rescued - isolate the near atom (1/n) log(1/d), then apply a49 to the reduced measure (1/(n-1)) sum over l != j,k of delta_{z_l}, which stays at distance >= eps/2 from z_-^{(k)} and is O(KS)-close to mu - but that argument is absent from the paper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the isolation argument: split off the nearest atom and apply a49 to the remaining (n-1)-point empirical measure.
issues.overall_effect: a50's upper bound (a53), and with it the upper-bound direction of Theorem a10, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Lemma a50's upper bound applies Lemma a49 at z_-^{(k)} without its distance hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The statement survives, but the proof needs a contained, nontrivial additional argument rather than a routine fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The key inequality U^{mu_k}(z_-^{(k)}) <= U^{mu_k}(a) requires a in supp(mu), because z_-^{(k)} minimizes only over supp(mu) while U^{mu_k}(z) -> -infinity off support as |z| -> infinity; the construction ensures only a notin the union of node balls and never addresses support membership. Moreover, the stated area argument does not produce any point: ball(z_-, (n+1)^{1/2}r) has area pi(n+1)r^2, exactly equal to the total area (n+1)pi r^2 of the n+1 excluded balls, so 'nonempty by considering the areas' is inconclusive (one must instead use (n+1)^{1/2}r < eps' << eps, so only O(1) node balls can meet the region). A workable repair needs a case analysis: if dist(z_-, S) > r, closedness of the union of node balls plus mu(ball(z_-, rho)) > 0 yields a in supp(mu) with dist(a, S) > r/2; if z_- lies within r of a node, the range of U^mu is small by the Holder condition and the bound is trivial since sup_z log L_k(z) >= log L_k(z_k) = 0.

failure_location.quote:
We pick $a$ to be any element of the set
\[\ball(z_-,(n+1)^{1/2}r)\backslash\bigcup_{j=0}^n\ball(z,r)\]
for $r=\frac1{2R}(\eps')^2$, which is nonempty by considering the areas of each ball.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry out the case analysis (support membership from closedness and positive mass of every neighborhood of z_-; the degenerate near-node case via the Holder condition and the trivial bound; replace the raw area comparison by a packing count).
issues.overall_effect: a50's lower bound, and with it the lower-bound direction of Theorem a10, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Lemma a50's lower bound: test point a not shown to lie in supp(mu); area comparison yields equal areas
issues.why_classification: The repair is a genuine new case analysis but leaves the statement and the rest of the paper untouched.
